summary: TrueMeter raised a $4M seed round led by Ulu Ventures (announced September 10, 2025), with backing also from Pear VC and e2.vc, bringing total funding to $5.5M+. Founded in 2023 by Stanford graduates Ali Sarilgan (CEO) and Dr. Ozge Islegen-Wojdyla. (Scope note: Full press release text returned a 403 on direct fetch; details corroborated via search-result summary of the same URL rather than a full read-through.)

Yoshinoya America is a named customer: per its VP of Finance, TrueMeter delivered '$200K+ savings each year,' consolidated 1,154 annual power bills into 12, and saved 68+ hours of accounting/tracking work. (Scope note: Savings figures are vendor-published and quote-attributed to the customer, but not independently audited.)

TrueMeter uses a performance-based pricing model: it is compensated as a share of savings it delivers and states it does not charge for savings from market price drops or reduced usage. Standard contracts run 12 months with cancellation available anytime; service requires an initial prepayment funded from historical usage to cover bill payment.
